RC3 adds optional experiments for read-only diagnosis, attention advice and selected history analysis.

- `workflow-diagnose` uses separately authorized read-only recipes, at most three child submissions,
  durable reservations, an absolute deadline, and existing workflow/process ownership. Status and
  wait remain non-dispatching. Diagnosis preserves the original failure; it does not repair an app.
- DL06 can advise on one eligible native-bound observation per run. It does not suppress notifications
  or change native delivery. Structured events need no classifier.
- DL12 adds explicitly requested history classification to native outcome reports. Stable analysis
  identities share the existing SQLite budget; completed analyses close their spent scopes.
- Assigned off/no-call episodes can be recorded and joined with treatment episodes. Reports retain
  failures, collection gaps and unknown usage. Version-1 outcome reports remain readable.

Every consumer remains optional and defaults off. No JEV account is required for ordinary operation.
Existing DL05 advice settings do not enable executable probes; that requires explicit `choose-read`
and separately approved host bindings. No predictive omission of required checks, live attention
suppression, model-tier routing, automatic repair or deployment is included.

Adopt this RC deliberately. New DL06/DL12 keys and version-2 manifests require this runtime. The first
explicit diagnostic write migrates the workflow ledger to engine schema 3; normal opens preserve
schema 2, and old binaries reject schema 3. Drain old runtime readers before adoption. After writes,
disable experiments and repair forward; do not restore an old ledger over new evidence.

Qualification covers deterministic source and installed-package fixtures, including native child
process execution with fixture inference. Live JEV quality and benefit, SDK adoption, and native
simulator/physical-device scenarios remain separate qualification work after publication. Simulator
observations in the new diagnostic entry describe the exact target after parent cleanup; they do not
prove its earlier app state. No token savings or device-readiness claim is made by this release.
